newsitem.title: THAILAND: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - March 3.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - March 3.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Thai press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- The House Committee on foreign affairs has played down criticism over accusations of disrespect to Army Commander-in-Chief General Chetta Thanajaro, regarding his appearance before the committee last week on the situation of Burmese refugees in Thailand. The criticism came from Gen Chetta's subordinates after only six of the House committee's 17 members showed up for the meeting at which the general was scheduled to give testimony over the reported relocation of the Karen to Burma. (THE NATION)

- Although the Star of Siam military satellite project has been virtually scrapped due to budget constraints, the Defence Ministry will continue to strive for a satellite system of its own by the year 2001. To stress the military's need for its own satellite system, Defence Permanent Secretary Gen Yuthasak Sasiprapha recently sent a letter to the cabinet secretary-general to reaffirm that the ministry had not given up the satellite project. (BANGKOK POST)

- Palang Dharma founder Chamlong Srimuang will not return to lead the strife-torn political party. Chamlong says he will leave the chance open to others but will join party meetings to help heal the rift between its former secretary-general Sudarat Keyuraphan and acting leader Chaiwat Sinsuwong. (BANGKOK POST)

- Termchai Pinyawatn has tendered his resignation as managing director of the financially-bankrupt Finance One Plc, which is bracing for a crisis today following its decision to seek a merger with the Thai Danu Bank, a financial source says. Termchai's resignation took place on Friday as the board of directors was meeting to discuss the best solution to save Thailand's largest finance company. (THE NATION)

- Deputy Prime Minister and Industry Minister Korn Dabaransi has ordered the Petroleum Authority of Thailand (PTT) to study two possible routes for a natural gas pipeline to the Northeast. He wants PTT to lay the pipeline simultaneously with a planned oil pipeline and fibre optic cable to reduce the high costs involved. (BUSINESS DAY)

- Giant foreign companies, taking advantage of reduced prices caused by the troubled Thai property industry, have approached the Nichada Thani Group of Companies about purchasing a 480 million baht luxury condominium. The 17-storey condominium is located in Bangkok's neighbouring province of Nonthaburi and is owned by the group's affiliate, Nichada Lake Shore West Co Ltd. (THE NATION)
